title: Tenant affinity, failure modes, and control-plane contracts
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact set of patterns and operational expectations for tenant routing across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. Focus is on: isolation boundaries, multi-region affinity, control-plane contract semantics (what the control plane promises to the data plane), and concrete failure/fallback behaviors operators should implement.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Tenants can be configured for Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Private (customer-owned VPC/on-prem).
- Each request carries: tenant-id, preferred-region list (optional), and SLA tier (e.g., standard/premium).
- Runtime supports model-variants with compatible fallbacks (quantized, smaller sequence-length profiled).
- Cookie-less (token-based) affinity — cannot rely on client IPs for strong affinity in private deployments.

High-level goals:
- Preserve isolation guarantees expected by each mode (strongest for Private, then Dedicated, weakest for Hosted).
- Keep the control-plane contract minimal and observable: if we promise affinity, we must expose metrics showing misses and fallbacks.
- Ensure predictable, auditable fallback sequence when capacity or network problems occur.

Control-plane contract (short):
- Placement decision: the control plane returns a routing descriptor (route-id, region, pool-type) and a TTL (seconds) for how long that placement is valid.
- Affinity vs. Fencing: the control plane indicates whether the returned placement is "fenced" (no cross-tenant co-location allowed) or "soft-affinity" (best-effort locality).
- Fallback policy: the control plane provides an ordered list of fallback candidates (model-variant + pool-type + region).
- Observability: every placement decision must emit events: placement.granted, placement.expired, placement.fallback(reason), placement.evicted(reason).

Policy primitives (pseudo):
- route = { tenant_id, pool_type, region, locality_kind, ttl, fallback_list }
- locality_kind in [fenced, soft, shared]

Example routing descriptor (text):
  tenant: acme-inc
  pool_type: dedicated
  region: us-west1
  locality_kind: fenced
  ttl: 300
  fallback_list:
    - { pool_type: dedicated, region: us-east1, locality_kind: fenced }
    - { pool_type: hosted, region: us-west1, locality_kind: shared }
    - { pool_type: hosted, region: global, locality_kind: shared }

Key mode-specific expectations and implications:
1) Private (strongest isolation)
- Expectation: control plane must never route a Private tenant into shared-hosted pools. Placement decisions are authoritative and require strict POSIX-like permission checks.
- Connectivity: runtime components may be customer-hosted; control-plane contract is an API handshake only. Latency to control plane can be variable; place longer TTLs (e.g., 10-30m) for Private to avoid churn.
- Fallback: fallbacks must point only to the customer's private clusters or a pre-approved secondary private region. No auto-fallback to hosted.
- Observability & audit: every cross-region/zone action must be logged for compliance.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Expectation: dedicated pools should give predictable throughput and soft tenancy isolation (no other tenant should be co-located on reserved nodes unless explicit oversubscription policy exists).
- Affinity: prefer fenced within the tenant's dedicated pool; allow geographic spillover to other dedicated pools in overflow scenarios before touching hosted.
- Fallback ordering recommendation: same-dedicated-region -> other-dedicated-region -> hosted (same region) -> hosted (global).
- Autoscale implications: scale-in/scale-out events must trigger placement.reassign with a short TTL so in-flight requests can be drained gracefully.

3) Hosted (multi-tenant shared)
- Expectation: most flexible and weakest isolation. Tenants accept co-location; control plane offers cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Affinity: soft-affinity; minimize cross-region traffic unless latency SLO allows.
- Fallback: allow model-variant downgrades (smaller quantized variant) before region changes to avoid egress.

Multi-region affinity strategies (patterns):
- Sticky-region affinity: prefer a single region with TTL; suitable for low-churn tenants. TTL longer for Private, shorter for Hosted.
- Geo-proximity: choose region from tenant.allowed_regions ordered by network latency measurements.
- Active-active preferred: keep healthy caches in both us-west/us-east, but keep a canonical placement in control plane.

Failure modes and recommended behaviors:
A) Control-plane timeout (data-plane could not get placement)
- Private: serve error to caller (fail closed) and page on-call. Rationale: customer expects direct control; wrong placements could break compliance.
- Dedicated: attempt conservative default: try last-known placement if TTL still valid, otherwise degrade to a secondary dedicated pool if policy allows.
- Hosted: fallback to global hosted pool with best-effort routing; increment placement.fallback events.

B) Region outage affecting place-holder pool
- Evict placement and pick first candidate from fallback_list. Emit placement.evicted with cause=region-unavailable. Update telemetry dashboards.

C) Overcommit detected (queue depth / CPU/GPU pressure)
- If tenant is premium and in Dedicated: trigger soft-throttle for low-priority tenants in same pool (but honor fenced contracts). If no soft options, spill to other dedicated region.
- If Hosted: auto-downgrade to quantized model variant as defined in fallback_list then spill to other region.

Operational runbook (quick):
- On placement.fallback spike (>5% of requests for 5m):
  - Check dedicated pool health metrics (utilization, queue latency).
  - Verify control-plane placement cache hit rate.
  - If spike is localized to a region, run region-resilience playbook (evacuate & warm target pool).
- On placement.evicted(reason=auth-failure):
  - Verify KMS/HSM key access (Private).
  - Do not auto-fallback to hosted. Page Security/SRE.

Example decision tree (short):
- Is tenant.Private? -> Yes -> enforce 'no-hosted' and longer TTLs -> on CP timeout: fail closed.
- Is tenant.Dedicated? -> Yes -> prefer dedicated fallback -> on capacity exhaustion: spill to dedicated-other-region -> if not available, consult oversubscription policy -> finally to hosted only with explicit customer permission.
- Else (Hosted) -> route to best-cost region, allow downgrades and hosted fallbacks.

Telemetry & SLOs to publish:
- placement.success_rate (by tenant, by mode)
- placement.fallback_rate (by fallback reason)
- affinity_miss_rate (requests not routed to preferred region)
- placement.ttl_expiry_rate (count how often TTLs force re-eval)
- cross-mode-fallback_count (important for billing/audit)

Notes to self / unresolved items:
- Need an explicit schema for "locality_kind" set and enforcement semantics in the runtime (what does fenced-mapping actually prevent?).
- Define a small, standard set of fallback-reasons for observability (e.g., capacity, region-unavailable, auth-failure, kernel-failure).
- Confirm legal/compliance constraints for Private -> Dedicated downscopes (should be disallowed in most cases).

Next steps / action items:
- (Ethan) propose a minimal placement descriptor JSON schema and publish to the control-plane API spec.
- (Priya) add telemetry dashboards for placement.fallback_rate by tenant segment.
- (Maya) draft an emergency fallback playbook for Dedicated -> Hosted transitions with billing implications annotated.

References / links:
- See linked artifacts above for current Confluence and PRs.

End of note.

(Informal style — this is intended as a compact engineering reference for the platform team; will expand into formal playbook after feedback.)
